en: Solid gallium metal will melt into a liquid puddle just by holding it in your warm hand.
A mixture of cornstarch and water becomes a solid when you punch it but flows like a liquid when you pour it.
When iron rusts, the resulting reddish-brown flaky material actually weighs more than the original solid iron because it absorbs oxygen from the air.
Rock candy crystals form because hot water dissolves more sugar than cold water, leaving excess sugar to crystallize as the syrup cools.
Unlike almost all other substances, water expands when it freezes, making solid ice less dense than liquid water so it floats.
The carbon dioxide gas produced when baking soda mixes with vinegar is heavier than air, allowing you to pour it like an invisible liquid.
Although it is a non-metal, a pure diamond conducts heat much faster than copper or silver because of its tightly bonded carbon atoms.
Solid carbon dioxide, called dry ice, skips the liquid state entirely and turns directly into an invisible gas at room temperature.
Soap molecules have one end that loves water and one end that loves oil, allowing them to trap grease and wash it away.
Heating white sugar causes a chemical change that breaks its molecules apart, creating hundreds of new complex flavors and a brown color called caramel.
Aerogel is a solid material made mostly of air, making it so light that a brick-sized piece weighs less than a smartphone.
The copper skin of the Statue of Liberty expands in summer heat and contracts in winter cold, changing its overall height by over an inch.
